_comment: A chain: a main store plus side structures that must agree with it. Each problem has two or more containers, every write touches more than one of them, and a read trusts the side structure only while the main store agrees. The two ways to make them agree are eager (fix the side structure on every write: 380, 146, 432, 460, 3508) and lazy (push a fresh entry, skip stale ones on read: 2349, 3885, 3408, 2034, 2353, 3815, 1172). Solve them in order, in a single sitting. state = what is stored, event = what happens on a call, invariant = what must be true between calls. Built 2026-10-08 from the cached editorials in research/doocs-leetcode. The ordering follows the clist rating.

2671.title: Frequency Tracker
2671.state: cnt: count per number; freq: how many numbers have each count
2671.event: add and deleteOne take the number out of its old count's bucket, change cnt, and put it in the new bucket
2671.invariant: freq[c] is the number of keys whose cnt is c

2349.title: Design a Number Container System
2349.state: index to number; per number a min-heap of its indices
2349.event: change overwrites the index's number and pushes the index on the new number's heap; find pops the heap top while the table says it holds another number
2349.invariant: the table is the truth; a heap entry is valid only while the table agrees with it
2349.change: the second structure is a heap per key instead of a counter, and stale entries are left in it and skipped on read

3885.title: Design Event Manager
3885.state: id to priority; a heap of (-priority, id)
3885.event: updatePriority writes the table and pushes a fresh pair; pollHighest pops the top while its priority disagrees with the table or the id is gone
3885.invariant: the top of the heap is answered only when the table still holds that priority for that id
3885.change: a single heap instead of a heap per key, with the same lazy skip

3829.title: Design Ride Sharing System
3829.state: a counter t; a sorted set of waiting riders and of free drivers as (t, id); rider id to its t
3829.event: add records (t, id) and bumps t; match pops the smallest t from both; cancel looks up the rider's t and removes that pair
3829.invariant: each waiting rider is in the set exactly once, under the t the table holds for it
3829.change: the side table exists so a delete by id can find its entry in the ordered set

3709.title: Design Exam Scores Tracker
3709.state: times: the record times in order; pre: prefix sums of the scores, same length plus 1
3709.event: record appends to both; totalScore binary-searches the two ends in times and subtracts the two prefix sums
3709.invariant: pre[i] is the sum of the first i scores, and times is sorted because records arrive in time order
3709.change: two lists appended in step instead of two dicts; the read is a range query by binary search

380.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
380.state: a list of the values; value to its index in the list
380.event: insert appends and records the index; remove moves the last value into the hole, fixes its index, and pops the end
380.invariant: d[v] is the index of v in the list, for every v in the list
380.change: a delete in the middle of the list is made O(1) by swapping with the last entry and repairing the index of the moved value

146.title: LRU Cache
146.state: key to node; a doubly linked list of the nodes in recency order
146.event: get moves the node to the front; put inserts at the front and evicts the tail over capacity
146.invariant: the dict and the list hold the same keys, and the list order is the recency order
146.change: the list stores an order instead of a position, so the side structure is a linked list and the dict points at nodes

2353.title: Design a Food Rating System
2353.state: food to (rating, cuisine); per cuisine a heap of (-rating, food)
2353.event: changeRating writes the table and pushes a fresh pair; highestRated pops the top while its rating disagrees with the table
2353.invariant: a heap entry is answered only when the table still holds that rating for that food
2353.change: the table carries two fields, and the heap key is a pair with a tie-break

3408.title: Design Task Manager
3408.state: task id to (user, priority); a heap of (-priority, -task id)
3408.event: add and edit write the table and push a fresh pair; rmv deletes from the table only; execTop pops while the top is gone or stale
3408.invariant: a heap entry is valid only while the table holds that task at that priority
3408.change: a delete arrives too; it touches the table only and the heap finds out on pop

2034.title: Stock Price Fluctuation
2034.state: price per timestamp, the latest timestamp, and a max-heap and min-heap of (price, timestamp)
2034.event: update overwrites the price for its timestamp and pushes on both heaps; maximum and minimum pop the top while it disagrees with the table
2034.invariant: a heap top is answered only when the table still holds that price at that timestamp
2034.change: two heaps over the same table, both read lazily

3508.title: Implement Router
3508.state: a set of the packets in the router, a FIFO deque with a capacity, and per destination a deque of timestamps
3508.event: add refuses a duplicate and evicts the front at capacity; forward pops the front; both pop the destination's timestamp deque too; getCount binary-searches that deque
3508.invariant: the set holds exactly the packets in the deque, and each destination's deque holds exactly its packets' timestamps, in order
3508.change: three structures; the side deques are popped eagerly, not lazily, because the packet leaving is always the oldest of its destination

3815.title: Design Auction System
3815.state: per item a heap of (-amount, user); per user and item the current amount
3815.event: add, update and remove write the user table and push a fresh pair; getHighestBidder pops while the top disagrees with the user table
3815.invariant: a heap entry is valid only while the user table holds that amount for that user and item
3815.change: the table is two levels deep, user then item, and a removed bid leaves a stale entry to skip

432.title: All O`one Data Structure
432.state: key to its bucket node; a doubly linked list of buckets in count order, each bucket a count and a set of keys
432.event: inc and dec move the key to the neighbouring bucket, creating it when missing and dropping a bucket that empties
432.invariant: buckets are in strictly increasing count order and no bucket is empty, so the ends are the min and max
432.change: the list holds groups of keys by count instead of single keys, and a key moves between neighbouring groups

381.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed
381.state: a list of the values; value to the set of its indices in the list
381.event: insert appends and adds the index; remove takes an index of the value, moves the last value into it, fixes that value's index set, and pops the end
381.invariant: d[v] is exactly the set of positions of v in the list
381.change: the index becomes a set of indices, and the swap must update the moved value's set before the removed value's set

460.title: LFU Cache
460.state: key to node; per count a doubly linked list of nodes in recency order; the smallest count in use
460.event: get and put move the node from its count's list to the next count's list; eviction pops the tail of the list for the smallest count
460.invariant: every key is in exactly the list of its count, and min_freq is the smallest non-empty count
460.change: the buckets are LRU lists, so the tie inside a count is broken by recency

895.title: Maximum Frequency Stack
895.state: count per value; per count a stack of the values that reached it; the largest count
895.event: push adds the value to the stack of its new count; pop takes from the stack of the largest count and lowers the count
895.invariant: the stack for count c holds, in push order, every value whose count is at least c
895.change: the count-of-counts becomes a stack per count, so a value sits in several stacks at once

1172.title: Dinner Plate Stacks
1172.state: a list of stacks; a min-heap of the indices of stacks that are not full
1172.event: push goes to the smallest not-full index; popAtStack adds the index back; pop drops empty stacks off the end
1172.invariant: every stack with room is in the heap, and no index past the last stack is answered
1172.change: the ordered side structure is a free list of slots, and entries past the end become stale
